static_traits.name: Li La
static_traits.family_status: Has a sister who plays guitar
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues are somewhat tense due to self-blame; has supportive family resources (sisters), but has not yet actively sought help
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; without prior psychotherapy; without obvious physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, capable of self-reflection, highly cooperative; neutral attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Because a student's English literature exam failure, I feel I am a useless teacher, experiencing a sense of incapability and self-blame.
basic_info.core_demands: This sense of incapability has affected my self-esteem and effective teaching ability, hence seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on students' grades

special_situations.event: The student's English literature exam failure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a student fails the exam, it means I am an incapable and incompetent teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately reflecting on and negating my teaching methods, seeking colleagues' feedback and planning to change teaching strategies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is all my fault; I am a useless teacher

special_situations.event: Seeing the failing result after exam grades were published
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure proves my overall teaching ability is insufficient
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling work, trying more one-on-one tutoring to make up for the 'failure'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One student's failure means I am not competent

special_situations.event: Encountering poor student performance or declining grades in teaching
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If any student performs poorly, it means my worth as a teacher drops to zero
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces leisure and relaxation; puts all energy into improving teaching
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not good enough/I failed

special_situations.event: The coexistence of positive feedback from successful students and one student's failure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only if all students perform well can it prove I am qualified; individual successes do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly focuses on failure cases and ignores positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those successes do not matter; I am still a useless teacher

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a competent and valuable teacher, with students progressing under my guidance
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as incapable, being blamed, or losing others' respect and professional worth
defense_goal: By over-taking responsibility and self-criticism, maintains a sense of control and avoids others' criticism

object_relations.self_representation: Blaming herself for student failure, worrying she is an incapable teacher
object_relations.object_representation: Students' grades and others' evaluations are experienced as harsh judges of her ability

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing or facing student exam failures and grade feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will blame her for the failure, and she must take full responsibility for students' grades
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaking in a low, self-blaming tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'it is all my fault', minimizing discussion of external factors, taking initiative to assume responsibility.

manifestations: Feeling 'all efforts are utterly meaningless' after the student failed
Feeling her teaching investment is negated by the failure outcome
outcomes: Difficulty enjoying knitting and other leisure activities

manifestations: Although having supportive sisters, still not confiding in them
Tense relationships with colleagues due to self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Treating 'student grades = teacher quality' as a must-follow standard
Stating 'I should be responsible for students' grades'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward others or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, turning it toward herself instead, redirecting outward libidinal energy against the self, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not seeking help from supportive sisters, turning to self-blame instead
Copes with feelings of failure by reducing leisure and self-punishment

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection abilities, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessively harsh on himself; repeatedly examines his own teaching methods
Still strongly doubts self when colleagues give positive feedback

positive_force: Having successful students who give positive feedback
Colleagues offering positive evaluations and support
Willing to reflect and try new teaching methods (e.g. one-on-one tutoring, adjusting materials)
Has a supportive sister who can provide emotional support
negative_force: Over-personalizing student grades as her own fault
Overgeneralizing one failure as overall incapability
Mental filtering: ignores positive evidence and success cases
Self-denial leading to tense relationships with colleagues and less leisure

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-blame and self-denying thoughts of 'I am a useless teacher' after poor student performance or exam failure
antecedent: Receiving exam scores or negative feedback
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly tying self-worth to student grades, with overgeneralization and personalization distortions
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a sense of control and trying to drive self-change through self-blame, avoiding facing uncertainty and external factors
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance,Tense relationships with colleagues,Low mood,Impaired self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Difficulty relaxing, reducing or being unable to enjoy leisure activities like knitting
antecedent: When self-blame and the sense of incapability persist
target_behavior.core_reason: Retroflection tendency driven by self-punishment and guilt
target_behavior.function: Restricting self-enjoyment to 'make up for mistakes' and relieve guilt
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased quality of life, reduced resilience, accumulating stress
